comparator.sourceNotes: The current curriculum is represented by its 45 separately credited compulsory study units totaling 150 EC, rather than ten opaque 15-EC parent labels. Genuine integrated project and academic-skills units remain intact; parents and children are never stacked. The third year preserves two generic 15-EC minor slots, Production Systems Engineering and the 12-EC research assignment plus 3-EC societal embedding.

core: Mathematical modelling, algorithms, signals and autonomous systems
Product requirements, prototyping and technological design
Life-cycle, material and resource consequences of technological systems

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields response passes the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. It combines mathematical system modelling, algorithms, data, robotics, product design, energy assessment, life-cycle analysis and resource technology. It is not represented as Mechanical Engineering. A separate structural/mechanical-design and manufacturing direction cannot supply statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics, elasticity, machine elements, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, tribology, manufacturing processes or the repeated build-and-test project sequence. A second energy-only route would reuse the existing energy strand while discarding the systems and design content that makes the accepted response coherent, so it was not included.

alternatives.label: Computational systems, robotics & sustainable technology
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical system models, algorithms, data methods and robotics alongside product design, life-cycle assessment, circular resource technology and renewable-energy analysis. This is a related-fields response; mechanical structures, thermal-fluid science, materials/manufacturing formation and engineering build-test projects remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is dominated by mathematics, computation and autonomous systems, with specific product-design, circular-material and renewable-energy strands. The label does not imply a Mechanical Engineering degree.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one and ten advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all later mathematics, robotics and neural-network work; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes recovery, resource and renewable-system study.

trace: uses a team-based design-and-development process with customer requirements, quantitative modelling, prototyping and fabrication-method choices; it does not supply a cumulative mechanical-design sequence
supplies programming, testing and debugging for implementing mathematical and autonomous-system models
establishes calculus, matrices, eigenvalues and differential equations for quantitative system models
develops vector spaces, matrices and linear transformations for coupled-system models
implements numerical methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations with accuracy and stability analysis
extends calculus to multiple dimensions, complex functions and differential equations for scientific and technological models
analyses linear systems through differential equations, transfer functions, state-space and signal-flow representations with control and signal-processing applications
develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertain measurements and model parameters
develops data preparation, visualisation and manipulation for technological investigations; it is a general data method rather than engineering measurement training
implements regression and statistical-learning methods for modelling and prediction in complex systems
processes image data through feature detection and tracking, with documented robotics and vehicle applications; it does not supply mechanical instrumentation
implements neural networks and deep learning for advanced visual and data models
studies robot kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance, manipulation and industrial automation without claiming mechanical construction or mechatronic hardware
develops and analyses algorithms and data structures for efficient computational systems
extends mathematical modelling and algorithm design to algebraic and optimisation problems
implements search, local/global optimisation and constraint satisfaction for complex computational design and planning problems
establishes documented physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability technologies
extends waves, chemistry and materials science through an applied sustainability case and prepares advanced resource and energy study
conducts advanced research on geothermal energy, carbon storage, waste storage and resource constraints
examines climate drivers, mitigation, renewable-energy systems and carbon storage as constraints on technology choices
evaluates environmental and health impacts of products, processes and services across their complete life cycle and develops circular alternatives
technically and economically assesses energy demand and solar, wind and bioenergy system designs for an external partner
examines recycling, recovery and remediation technologies, resource security, materials and laboratory work for circular technological systems
blocks: Both introduce programming for modelling and technical problem solving; UCR supplies general Python programming rather than the external engineering-modelling sequence.
Both establish calculus foundations for quantitative engineering models; the external component belongs to a longer engineering-mathematics sequence.
Both directly study matrices, vectors and linear algebra for system representation.
Both extend calculus and differential-equation methods; UCR is general mathematical study rather than embedded mechanical analysis.
Both analyse systems through mathematical models; UCR covers linear systems, transfer functions and state-space without the full engineering context.
Both provide probability/statistics for quantitative modelling and research.

The external project analyses and redesigns integrated mechanical/mechatronic systems. Computational robot kinematics and motion planning do not establish an important part of this project's specified hardware/system-redesign work; Robotics remains complementary study.

General root-finding, interpolation, numerical integration and ordinary-differential-equation algorithms provide foundations but do not establish finite-element discretisation or finite-element analysis. No direct finite-element method is evidenced in the selected UCR course.
Both use a team design process involving requirements, prototyping and product development; UCR does not reproduce mechanical-tool design or the target’s cumulative engineering-project sequence.
Energy, life cycles, materials and resources
Both directly evaluate environmental impacts across product or process life cycles.

Both directly analyse an energy system and assess technical choices. UCR evaluates energy use and renewable options with technical/economic analysis and a partner report; it does not reproduce the external project's material and thermodynamic engineering analysis.

notes.text: The UCR programme provides substantial mathematical, computational, robotic, product-design and sustainable-technology study. It does not supply the target’s cumulative mechanics, thermodynamics, materials/manufacturing, thermal-fluid, machine-design, laboratory and build-test formation and is not a Mechanical Engineering qualification.
